quotes.text: The ability of a segment of a glass sphere to magnify whatever is placed before it was known around the year 1000, when the spherical segment was called a reading stone,[…]. Scribes, illuminators, and scholars held such stones directly over manuscript pages as an aid in seeing what was being written, drawn, or read.
quotes.reference: 2013 September-October, Henry Petroski, “The Evolution of Eyeglasses”, in American Scientist:

subsenses.definition: (of a person or person's face) Appearing tired and unwell, as from stress; haggard.

quotes.text: The lean, drawn starvelings in their dream-stupefied state were jealous of my well filled out, prosperous form.
quotes.reference: 1924 July 25 [1923 August 25], Samuel Badisch Ornitz, “Fifth Period”, in Haunch Paunch and Jowl, eighth printing, New York, N.Y.: Boni and Liveright, section III, page 218:

senses.definition: (of a game) Undecided; having no definite winner and loser; at a draw.
(in combination) Pulled, towed, or extracted in the specified fashion.
